parameters.label: King range
parameters.description: How many squares the King may move in one straight direction.
parameters.notes: Higher values change what counts as an attack. Fairness plan: test 1 if the draw rate is high.

parameters.label: King can jump
parameters.description: Whether the King may pass over an occupied first square.

parameters.label: King can enter the Coast
parameters.description: Whether a King may move onto Coast squares (file A).

parameters.label: Castling
parameters.description: Whether castling is allowed. When on, it works as in chess: the King moves 2 squares toward an unmoved Rook, which lands on the square the King crossed.

parameters.label: Queen can enter void squares
parameters.description: Whether the Queen may land on or pass through the void squares B5, C5, D5, F5, G5 and H5.
parameters.notes: Replaced in S40 by queen.canCrossVoid and queen.canStandOnVoid (owner, 24 Oct 2026); true is both of them on. Kept so the registry still names it; rulesets that set it moved to the two new switches in a new version (easy-2p 0.2.0).

parameters.label: Queen crosses the void
parameters.description: Whether the Queen may pass over the empty void squares B5, C5, D5, F5, G5 and H5 on her way to a square beyond them. It doesn't let her stop on one (queen.canStandOnVoid).
parameters.notes: Default false is today's behavior (queen.canEnterVoid false). With queen.canStandOnVoid it replaces queen.canEnterVoid. Rank 5 still never crosses e5 sideways (her piece data).

parameters.label: Queen may stand on a void square
parameters.description: Whether the Queen may stop on, or capture on, a void square B5, C5, D5, F5, G5 or H5. It doesn't let her pass over one (queen.canCrossVoid).

optionLabels.false: Never stops on a void square
optionLabels.true: May stop on a void square

parameters.notes: Default false is today's behavior (queen.canEnterVoid false). With queen.canCrossVoid it replaces queen.canEnterVoid.

parameters.label: Queen void crossings
parameters.description: Where the Queen may cross the void: A5 and I5 (may stop) and E5 (pass over only, when empty), only E5, or nowhere.
parameters.notes: Replaces queen.enemyTerritoryEntry. E5 is crossed only along the E-file and the diagonals D4-F6 and F4-D6.

parameters.label: Queen can enter the Coast
parameters.description: Whether a Queen may move onto Coast squares (file A).

parameters.label: Queen and green pawn swap
parameters.description: Once per game, as her move, a Queen may trade squares with her green pawn (starts on E2 or E8), when both pieces may legally stand on their new squares and her King is not left in check. A pawn swapped onto its promotion rank promotes at once.

parameters.label: Pawn double step
parameters.description: Whether a standard pawn may advance two squares on its first move.

optionLabels.true: Two squares on the first move

parameters.label: Pawn promotion targets
parameters.description: Which pieces an eligible pawn may promote to. The option captured-piece adds any piece type its side has lost (queen, rook, bishop, knight or Coast piece); if the side has lost none, the pawn stays a pawn.
parameters.notes: Default from decision D2. Light pawns promote on rank 9, dark pawns on rank 1. captured-piece is off by default; meaning given by the owner on 19 Oct 2026 (S14). Provisional readings: combined with other options it adds the lost pieces to them, and Kings and pawns are never targets.

parameters.label: Pawn-safe zones
parameters.description: A pawn that has crossed the void can't be captured on the opponent's colored square in its own starting file (B2/B8, C3/C7, D4/D6, F4/F6, G3/G7, H2/H8). It can still move, capture and give check.

optionLabels.starting-file: Colored square of its starting file

parameters.notes: Board data for the colored squares arrives with S10. E-file and I-file pawns have no safe zone.

parameters.label: Pawns may enter the Coast
parameters.description: Whether a pawn may enter the Coast (file A) once it is open. It gets there only by capturing onto file A, then moves forward along file A and promotes on its last rank as usual.
parameters.notes: Default false is today's behavior. Reading from decision default D45 (provisional): a pawn moves straight forward, so its only way onto file A is a diagonal capture from file B; on file A it steps forward (A5 when empty) and captures diagonally back onto file B. While the Coast is closed nothing but the Tail moves to or from it (game state).

parameters.label: Pawns may enter E5
parameters.description: Whether a pawn may move onto the center square E5.

parameters.label: Who may stand on E5
parameters.description: Which pieces may occupy the center square E5.
parameters.notes: dragons = both Dragon Heads and the Dragon Tail.

parameters.label: Who may pass over E5
parameters.description: Which pieces may pass over an empty E5 in a straight line or jump. No piece passes through an occupied E5.
parameters.notes: Rooks and Bishops can't slide through E5 by default.

parameters.label: Opening the Coast (2-player)
parameters.description: How the Coast opens in 2-player games: a player moves the Dragon Tail from A5 to E5, or the Coast is open from the start. Once open it stays open.

parameters.label: Leaving the Coast (2-player)
parameters.description: How Coast pieces leave the Coast in 2-player games once it is open.

parameters.label: Leaving the Coast (3-player)
parameters.description: How Coast pieces leave the Coast in 3-player games: first emergence through A5, then any legal move, or always through A5.
parameters.notes: While on the Coast, the Sun and Moon move one square at a time.

parameters.label: Every piece may enter the Coast
parameters.description: Whether every piece may enter the Coast at any time: the Coast is open from the start, so Coast pieces may move from the first turn, and no piece's own Coast setting (Kings, Queens, pawns) or Coast bar (Rooks, Bishops, Knights) keeps it off file A.

optionLabels.true: Every piece, from the first turn

parameters.notes: Default false is today's behavior. Meaning from decision default D44 (provisional). Provisional reading (S40): it lifts the rules that keep a piece from entering the Coast, not the Coast pieces' own ways off and back (coast.2p.exit, coast.returnAllowed) or the Queen's void crossings (queen.voidCrossings closes a5 to her). 3-player Coast opening is not built.

parameters.label: Coast pieces may return
parameters.description: Whether Coast pieces may move back onto the Coast after leaving it.

parameters.label: Capture on the Coast (2-player)
parameters.description: Whether Coast pieces standing on the Coast can be captured in 2-player games. The Tail is never captured.

parameters.label: Capture on the Coast (3-player)
parameters.description: Whether Coast pieces standing on the Coast can be captured in 3-player games.

parameters.label: Dragon Tail squares (2-player)
parameters.description: Where the Tail may stand in 2-player games. It jumps, so pieces in between don't block it.
parameters.notes: First move is always A5 to E5, which opens the Coast.

parameters.label: Dragon Tail movement (3-player)
parameters.description: How the Tail moves in 3-player games: any direction, any distance, like a Dragon Head, or the 2-player path.

parameters.label: Tail repeat limit
parameters.description: How many of a player's own turns in a row may be Tail moves (0 = no limit). The player who opens the Coast may move the Tail A5 to E5 and then E5 to I5 on consecutive turns, the first time.
parameters.notes: Stops the Tail being used as a free pass.

parameters.label: Dragon Tail captures (2-player)
parameters.description: Whether the Tail may capture in 2-player games.
parameters.notes: Even when on, the Tail never captures a piece of the side moving it (owner, 19 Oct 2026, S17).

parameters.label: Dragon Tail captures (3-player)
parameters.description: What the Tail may capture in 3-player games.

parameters.label: Dragon Tail gives check
parameters.description: Whether the Tail can check a King.

parameters.label: Dragon Tail can be captured
parameters.description: Whether the Tail can be captured. In 3-player games the capturing piece switches places with the Tail, which turns to stone, handled as a checkmate of the Tail (decision 0018).

parameters.label: Dragon Head range
parameters.description: How many squares a Dragon Head may slide in one straight direction. 8 is unlimited on a 9x9 board.
parameters.notes: Fairness plan: test 3 and 4 against unlimited.

parameters.label: Coast piece range mode
parameters.description: How range is counted for all 5 Coast pieces: squares in one straight line, stopping when blocked.
parameters.notes: Decision D4. The owner removed the turn-a-corner (moves) option.

parameters.label: Dragon Heads can jump
parameters.description: Whether a Dragon Head may pass over occupied squares.

parameters.label: Coast pieces give check (2-player)
parameters.description: Whether Dragon Heads and the Sun and Moon give check in 2-player games.

parameters.label: Dragon gives check (3-player)
parameters.description: Whether the Dragon player's pieces give check to Kings. When off, the Dragon may instead capture an attacked King.

parameters.label: Sun and Moon range (2-player)
parameters.description: How many squares a Sun or Moon may move in one straight direction in 2-player games.

parameters.label: Sun and Moon first move (2-player)
parameters.description: Whether a Sun or Moon may move 2 squares straight forward on its first move.

optionLabels.true: Two squares on the first move

parameters.label: Sun and Moon range off the Coast (3-player)
parameters.description: How many squares a Sun or Moon may move in one straight direction once off the Coast in 3-player games. On the Coast it moves one square at a time.

parameters.label: Sun and Moon capture
parameters.description: How a Sun or Moon captures.

optionLabels.any-move-square: Any square it can move to

parameters.notes: Decision D6. any-move-square = it captures onto any square it can move to.

parameters.label: Sun and Moon promotion
parameters.description: Whether a Sun or Moon may promote.

parameters.label: First move (2-player)
parameters.description: Which side moves first in 2-player games. In 3-player games the order is dark, light, Dragon.
parameters.notes: Decision D26.

parameters.label: Stalemate result (2-player)
parameters.description: The result when the player to move has no legal move and is not in check.

parameters.label: Stalemate result (3-player)
parameters.description: A Kinged player who is not in check and has no legal move on their turn ends the game as a draw between the two Kinged players.

parameters.label: How 3-player games end
parameters.description: The full Dragon rules (stones, the Tail in stone and the duel), or the first checkmate wins: a Kinged player wins by checkmating the other King or the Tail, the Dragon by checkmating either King.
parameters.notes: first-checkmate needs dragon.3p.givesCheck on; the loader refuses a ruleset that sets one without the other.

parameters.label: The Dragon's win in the duel
parameters.description: Once the Dragon has captured one King: Dragon attacks on the last King are check and the Dragon wins by checkmating it, or Dragon attacks follow dragon.3p.givesCheck and the Dragon wins by capturing it.
parameters.notes: Applies with endings.3p = stones-and-duel.

parameters.label: When the Tail is checkmated
parameters.description: Right after the move that checkmates it, or only if, at the start of the Dragon's turn, it is attacked and the Dragon has no move that ends the attack.
parameters.notes: Applies with endings.3p = stones-and-duel.

parameters.label: Threefold repetition (3-player)
parameters.description: Whether the same position (stones and seat statuses included) with the same player to move, for the third time, is a draw.

parameters.label: Fifty-move rule (3-player)
parameters.description: Whether 50 moves by every player still in the game, with no capture, pawn move, King captured or piece turned to stone, is a draw. Tail, Sun and Moon moves count as moves.

parameters.label: A King left in check for an earlier player
parameters.description: Whether a move may leave a King in check from a player who moves before that King's owner can answer. If it may, the King's owner loses at once to the owner of the piece giving check.

parameters.label: Threefold repetition
parameters.description: Whether threefold repetition is a draw. Tail moves count as moves.

parameters.label: Fifty-move rule
parameters.description: Whether 50 moves by each side with no capture or pawn move is a draw. Tail moves count as moves.

parameters.label: Insufficient material
parameters.description: Whether a position where neither side can checkmate is a draw.

parameters.label: Swap King and Queen start
parameters.description: Kings start on E1/E9 (white squares) and Queens on F1/F9 instead.
parameters.notes: Decision D30. Not for tournaments until tested and ratified.

parameters.label: Extended play (3-player)
parameters.description: After a King checkmates the other, the Dragon may play on with captured pieces if both remaining players agree. Terms not yet settled.
parameters.notes: Decision D31, set aside. Captured pieces re-enter through A5.

parameters.label: Queen entry into enemy territory
parameters.description: Whether the Queen may enter the opponent's half only through gateway squares or anywhere.
parameters.notes: Replaced by queen.voidCrossings in rule set v0.2.

parameters.label: Dragon range
parameters.description: How far a Dragon may move in one move.
parameters.notes: Replaced by dragonHead.range (Heads) and tail.3p.movement (Tail) in rule set v0.2.

parameters.label: Dragons in 2-player games
parameters.description: Whether frozen Dragons block their starting squares or are removed from the board.
parameters.notes: Superseded in rule set v0.2: Coast pieces play in 2-player games (see coast.2p.initiation).
